summary: CLAIM C-0005: ESTABLISHED — hypnotic inductions produce real changes in subjective experience and brain activity, BUT they are not necessary for suggestion responses and only modestly increase responsiveness. The strong/traditional 'trance required' (qualitative state) view is rejected by current evidence.
content: CLAIM C-0005: What is established vs contested — ESTABLISHED: (1) Hypnotic inductions produce genuine, measurable changes in subjective experience and brain activity (not faked — EV-0013). (2) Hypnotic inductions are NOT necessary for suggestion responses and only modestly increase responsiveness; 54% are equally or less suggestible post-induction (EV-0004, EV-0012). (3) The strong/traditional QUALITATIVE STATE hypothesis (trance is REQUIRED for suggested perceptual changes) is rejected by converging evidence (EV-0013). (4) Hypnotic analgesia efficacy is robust and broadly agreed (EV-0011). CONTESTED: whether induction-produced brain changes reflect a UNIQUELY hypnotic state vs mundane processes; whether the state construct has causal vs merely descriptive/epiphenomenal status.
